q: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called ____.
e: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called vaporization. The name used here is vaporization.

q: The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its boiling point.

q: Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the ____ $L_v$ of the liquid.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of vaporization L_v of the liquid.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is ____ $J kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2 255 176 J kg^-1.

q: But ____ $J kg^{-1}$ will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of vaporization of water.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. But 2.255 × 10^6 J kg^-1 will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of vaporization of water.

q: The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called ____.
e: The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called condensation. The name used here is condensation.
Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In condensation, the substance releases heat.
Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In vaporization, the substance absorbs heat.
